sub_graphs.title: EIP-1872: Network Upgrade Scheduling Framework
sub_graphs.description: Models the decision process for scheduling different types of network upgrades

nodes.label: Network Upgrade Proposed
nodes.description: A network upgrade has been proposed and needs classification

nodes.label: Classify Upgrade Type
nodes.description: Determine if upgrade is Roadmap, Priority, or Critical based on urgency and risk

nodes.label: Upgrade Classified as Roadmap
nodes.description: Upgrade is a deliberate protocol improvement without urgency

nodes.label: Upgrade Classified as Priority
nodes.description: Upgrade requires urgency but without systemic risk

nodes.label: Upgrade Classified as Critical
nodes.description: Upgrade is an emergency response to systemic risk

nodes.label: Select Roadmap Window
nodes.description: Choose from quarterly windows: third Wednesday of January, April, July, or October

nodes.label: Select Priority Window
nodes.description: Use any unused roadmap window (third week of any month)

nodes.label: Deploy Critical Upgrade
nodes.description: Deploy immediately without scheduling constraints

nodes.label: Upgrade Window Selected
nodes.description: An activation window has been selected for the upgrade

external_entities.name: Ethereum Core Developers
external_entities.description: Development teams proposing and coordinating network upgrades

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1872: Block Number Selection Convention
sub_graphs.description: Models the process for selecting activation block numbers for network upgrades

nodes.label: Upgrade Window Confirmed
nodes.description: A target window (week) has been selected for the upgrade

nodes.label: Estimate Target Block Number
nodes.description: Calculate block number that will be mined around Wednesday 12:00 UTC of target week

nodes.label: Apply Block Number Convention
nodes.description: For mainnet: choose number ending with 000 or more zeros; for testnets: choose palindromic number

nodes.label: Activation Block Selected
nodes.description: A specific block number has been chosen for the upgrade activation

nodes.label: Announce Activation Block
nodes.description: Publicly announce the chosen block number for client updates

nodes.label: Upgrade Scheduled
nodes.description: Upgrade is officially scheduled with block number and clients can implement

external_entities.name: Client Development Teams
external_entities.description: Teams implementing the upgrade in Ethereum client software

external_entities.name: Node Operators
external_entities.description: Operators who must update their nodes before the activation block

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1872: Upgrade Cadence Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation rules for upgrade scheduling cadence

nodes.label: Upgrade Cadence Proposed
nodes.description: A cadence (time between upgrades) has been proposed

nodes.label: Validate Cadence Multiple
nodes.description: Check if cadence is a multiple of 3 months (3, 6, 9, 12 months)

nodes.label: Cadence Valid
nodes.description: Proposed cadence meets the multiple-of-3-months requirement

nodes.label: Cadence Invalid
nodes.description: Proposed cadence does not meet requirements (e.g., 4 or 5 months)

nodes.label: Check Consecutive Windows
nodes.description: Verify that consecutive roadmap windows are not used

nodes.label: Scheduling Approved
nodes.description: Upgrade scheduling passes all validation rules

ambiguities.text: The definition of 'systemic risk' that distinguishes Priority from Critical upgrades is not precisely defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume systemic risk means risk of widespread network disruption, fund loss, or consensus failure affecting the majority of users

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define what happens if an upgrade is proposed close to but after the lead time window
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the upgrade must wait for the next available window that meets lead time requirements

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'production grade networks' is used without a clear definition
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume production grade networks are mainnet and any testnet with significant economic value or user base

implicit_assumptions.description: Block times are predictable enough to estimate block numbers weeks in advance
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Upgrades could activate significantly earlier or later than the target window, causing coordination problems

implicit_assumptions.description: The core development community will adhere to this scheduling framework consistently
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Unpredictable upgrade schedules could harm ecosystem stability and user trust

implicit_assumptions.description: Node operators have sufficient time (2-6 weeks) to update their software
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Significant portion of network could fail to upgrade, causing chain splits
